MERIDIAN CARD SERVICES — DISPUTES OPERATIONS
CASE REVIEW PACKET: DISPUTE DP-26-0703318 (PAXNET CREDIT CARD)

=== EXCERPT 1: PAXNET DISPUTE RULES FOR ISSUERS (EDITION APRIL 2026), CHAPTER 9 ===

9.0 General
9.0.1 The issuer may raise a dispute on behalf of a cardholder only under a valid reason code and within the time limits of that reason code. Rules in this chapter are to be applied by the issuer's dispute analyst at each stage (initial dispute, pre-arbitration). The analyst's decision at the representment review stage is whether the dispute is decided in the cardholder's favour (the provisional credit is made final and the merchant is debited) or in the merchant's favour (the provisional credit is reversed).
9.0.2 Days are calendar days unless stated otherwise.
9.0.3 A merchant's compelling evidence must be assessed against the specific requirements of the reason code; general statements ("the item was shipped", "the customer is a repeat buyer") are not compelling evidence.

9.1 Reason code 13.1 — Merchandise or services not received
9.1.1 Use: the cardholder paid for merchandise or services that were not received by the agreed date or location.
9.1.2 Pre-conditions: (a) the cardholder attempted to resolve the dispute with the merchant, and either the merchant refused, did not respond within 7 days, or the merchant is no longer trading; (b) the cardholder has not received the merchandise at the time of the dispute.
9.1.3 Time limit: the dispute must be raised within 120 days of the expected delivery date where the purchase terms stated an expected delivery date or a latest delivery date; otherwise within 120 days of the transaction processing date. In any case not later than 540 days after the transaction processing date.
9.1.4 Merchant compelling evidence (representment) is limited to:
   (a) proof of delivery to the address given by the cardholder at the time of purchase, such as carrier tracking showing delivery to that address;
   (b) proof of delivery to a collection point, parcel locker or other pickup location, but only where (i) the cardholder selected that pickup location at checkout or later authorised the change in writing, or (ii) the merchant also provides evidence that the cardholder or a person authorised by the cardholder collected the item (for example a locker log showing collection with the cardholder's PIN, or a signed pickup receipt);
   (c) evidence that the cardholder has used the merchandise or services (for example online account activity for digital goods);
   (d) evidence that the cardholder agreed to a new delivery date that has not yet passed.
9.1.5 A carrier-initiated redirection of a parcel (for example after a failed delivery attempt) does not by itself constitute the cardholder's selection or authorisation of the pickup location, even if the carrier notified the cardholder by email or text message.
9.1.6 A merchant offer to re-ship or refund made after the dispute has been raised does not invalidate the dispute unless the cardholder accepts it.

9.2 Reason code 13.3 — Not as described or defective merchandise
9.2.1 The cardholder must have returned or attempted to return the merchandise, unless the merchant refused to provide return instructions.
9.2.2 Time limit: 120 days from the date of receipt of the merchandise.

9.3 Reason code 13.6 — Credit not processed
9.3.1 Use where the merchant provided a credit voucher or a refund acknowledgement that was not processed. Time limit: 120 days from the date on the credit acknowledgement; if undated, 120 days from the date of the cardholder's return of the goods.

9.4 Reason code 10.4 — Card-absent fraud
9.4.1 The cardholder must certify that they did not authorise or participate in the transaction. Transactions authenticated with strong customer authentication are generally not eligible.

=== EXCERPT 2: PAXNET MEMBER BULLETIN 2026-11 (EFFECTIVE 1 JUNE 2026) ===
(1) For reason code 13.1, signature on delivery is no longer required as part of proof of delivery under 9.1.4(a) for transactions below EUR 250. For transactions of EUR 250 or more, carrier tracking with GPS or photo evidence of delivery at the address is sufficient.
(2) Time limits in 9.1.3 are unchanged.
(3) Reason code 13.3 now allows photographic evidence of defects in place of an independent expert opinion for goods under EUR 1,000.

=== EXCERPT 3: MERIDIAN INTERNAL PROCEDURE DSP-04 (DISPUTE ANALYST DESK GUIDE) ===
- Provisional credit is granted to the cardholder when a dispute is raised and remains in place until the representment review.
- The analyst records the outcome as "Cardholder favour" or "Merchant favour" with the rule reference.
- Fees: Paxnet charges the issuer EUR 15 per pre-arbitration filing; this does not affect the analyst's decision.
- Where the analyst cannot decide on the evidence, request more information from the cardholder with a 10-day deadline (not needed where the rules decide the case).
- Communications: the cardholder is informed of the outcome by secure message within 2 business days of the decision, with a plain-language explanation. Do not quote Paxnet rule numbers to the cardholder.
- Repeat disputers: cardholders with more than three disputes in 12 months are referred to the Card Risk team after the case is decided; this referral never changes the outcome of an individual dispute.
- Merchant contact: analysts must not contact the merchant directly; all communication goes through the Paxnet dispute platform.
- Service level: representment reviews are completed within 5 business days of receipt of the representment.

=== CASE FILE DP-26-0703318 ===
Cardholder: Mr Oskar Lindqvist-Barre, card ending 4471 (Meridian Platinum).
Merchant: Soundhaven Audio Online (merchant category 5732, electronics), merchant ID SH-99210.
Transaction: 2 March 2026, EUR 389.00, "AuraSound X9 wireless headphones — PRE-ORDER". Transaction processing date: 2 March 2026. 3-D Secure authenticated.
Order confirmation (supplied by cardholder): order SH-2026-118830; "Pre-order: ships no later than 20 March 2026; expected delivery by 20 March 2026." Delivery method selected at checkout: "Standard home delivery" to Flat 3, 14 Harbour Mews, Lindhaven. Pickup/locker options were available at checkout but not selected.

Cardholder statement (dispute form, 11 July 2026):
"I never received the headphones. In late March I got a text from the carrier saying a delivery attempt failed and the parcel was at a ParcelPoint locker, but I was abroad on business until 9 April and by then the tracking said 'returned to sender'. I assumed Soundhaven would refund me. I emailed them on 28 June 2026 asking for my money back or the headphones and got no reply. I did not authorise any redirection."
Cardholder's email to merchant of 28 June 2026: attached (sent to support@soundhaven-example.com; no reply recorded).
Dispute raised by Meridian: 11 July 2026, reason code 13.1. Provisional credit EUR 389.00 posted 11 July 2026.

Merchant representment (received 29 July 2026):
"The order was shipped on 18 March 2026 with tracking number PP-7730-44812. The carrier attempted delivery on 23 March and, as the customer was not home, redirected the parcel to ParcelPoint locker #4471 (Station Square, Lindhaven) on 24 March. The carrier notified the customer by text message with the collection PIN. Delivery was therefore completed. In addition the dispute is late — it was raised 131 days after the transaction. Finally, on 15 July 2026 we offered to re-ship the headphones free of charge, which the customer ignored. We request reversal of the dispute."
Attachments: carrier tracking history; screenshot of carrier SMS template; email of 15 July 2026 offering reshipment.

Carrier tracking history (from representment):
18 Mar 2026 16:02 — Shipment received by carrier
23 Mar 2026 11:47 — Delivery attempted, recipient not available (Harbour Mews)
24 Mar 2026 08:15 — Redirected by carrier to ParcelPoint locker #4471, Station Square
24 Mar 2026 09:30 — Delivered to locker; collection PIN sent to recipient
31 Mar 2026 18:00 — Not collected within 7-day storage period; returning to sender
04 Apr 2026 10:12 — Returned to sender (Soundhaven warehouse)

Cardholder reply to the 15 July offer (forwarded to Meridian 20 July 2026): "No thank you — I bought a different pair months ago. I want the refund."

Previous disputes by this cardholder: one in 2023 (reason 10.4, card-absent fraud, decided in cardholder favour). No disputes with this merchant before.
Analyst assignment: representment review opened 30 July 2026.

decision.instructions: At the representment review stage, should dispute DP-26-0703318 be decided in the cardholder's favour under the Paxnet rules?

criteria.false: The dispute is invalid (e.g. late or pre-conditions unmet) or the merchant supplied compelling evidence, so the credit is reversed.
criteria.true: The dispute was validly raised and the merchant's representment does not contain compelling evidence under the rules, so the cardholder keeps the credit.
